messages:
alex_cs: FYI — CedarHealth (Dedicated) reported a reproducible issue that looks like long-tail token-level latency and occasional 502s when prefetch is enabled. customer says cost spike too. repro steps below.

sam_support: thanks alex — can you drop the minimal repro and the earliest logs we have? cc @kai_eng for runtime triage.

alex_cs: pasted minimal repro from the customer (they ran this against our dedicated pool in us-west-2):

```
# reproduce (customer environment)
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "redwood-dedicated-bert-qa-1.2",
  "prefetch": true,
  "input": "Explain the steps for post-op care in simple bullet points",
  "max_tokens": 600,
  "session_id": "cedar-12345"
}
```

alex_cs: Observed behavior: first ~3 requests are fine (p95 ~220ms). then token generation stalls intermittently (token latency jumps to 2-6s) for the next 60-90s and a small fraction of requests return 502s. Customer sees KV cache hits drop during the window. They say disabling `prefetch` removes the long-tail.

kai_eng: can you include the request id / trace id from one of the failed requests? need to correlate with runtime logs. Also which runtime version? @alex_cs

alex_cs: one sample trace id: trace=tr-20260304-cedar-9f7a (from their header). Runtime reported by customer: commit sha `a1b2c3f` (from the agent) — they said host AMI redwood-dedicated-2026-02-14.

jules_sre: pasting quick grep from the runtime logs at the time (customer redacted hostnames):

```
[2026-03-04T21:12:03Z] trace=tr-20260304-cedar-9f7a session=cedar-12345 kvcache: hit=0 miss=18
[2026-03-04T21:12:04Z] trace=tr-20260304-cedar-9f7a token_gen: latency=230ms
[2026-03-04T21:12:10Z] trace=tr-20260304-cedar-9f7a token_gen: latency=3200ms
[2026-03-04T21:12:12Z] trace=tr-20260304-cedar-9f7a ERROR downstream: http 502 upstream timeout
```

jules_sre: looks like a KV cache churn (misses up) when prefetch is on. could be eviction thrash or a prefetch race.

maria_pm: quick prioritization check — CedarHealth is on an enterprise reserved contract (monthly committed). They flagged impact on billing and SLA. They asked for a timeline. How severe is this for other customers? @kai_eng

kai_eng: initial read = medium-high severity for Dedicated customers that enable prefetch. We need to confirm whether this is a config/regression (kernel selection / kvcache interface) or customer-specific (their workload pattern). Suggest steps: 1) replicate internally against same runtime sha and model, with prefetch ON/off. 2) attach profiler (token-level timing) and runtime debug logs. 3) if reproducible, prioritize a patch and release.

sam_support: I've created a Jira ticket and linked it to the customer's case: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RI-4682 (internal) — assigned to eng-runtime backlog for now.

alex_cs: customer asked for a workaround before patch. they are fine with disabling prefetch but want minimal perf impact. any config we can push as a temporary mitigation?

kai_eng: short-term: toggle `prefetch=false` on their Dedicated pool (we can do config override per-pool). That reduces throughput a bit but prevents cache thrash. Long-term: we need to add a guard in prefetch logic to avoid simultaneous full-kv repopulation under high concurrency.

maria_pm: please mark product-impact and customer-comms in the Jira. If this requires behavior change in prefetch, add rollout criteria: unit tests reproducing thrash, canary on non-prod pools, and compatibility test for existing sessions.

jules_sre: added the logs and a flamegraph from the customer's profile to the ticket (obf). note: we saw repeated `kv_evict` ops during the window.

kai_eng: can someone from CS get a short snippet of the exact workload pattern they sent (traffic rate + concurrency) — that matters for repro.

alex_cs: customer traffic: sustained 15 qps, 3 concurrent sessions, burstiness around 50 qps for <30s every ~10 minutes. they included sample sequence lengths ~ avg 120 tokens.

devops-bot: Incident created: #RI-4682 (priority=P2). Pager=false.

sam_support: adding triage notes: reproducible with our internal stress tool if we replicate their burst pattern plus prefetch=true. putting request into eng-runtime sprint backlog for next triage meeting.

kai_eng: I'll try to reproduce today. if I can replicate, I'll open a PR with a mitigation flag and tests. tagging @maria_pm for timeline.

maria_pm: thanks — if we have a repro + PR within 3 business days, we can schedule a hotfix for next patch release and inform CedarHealth. Otherwise we scope to the next minor release and provide a mitigations doc to the customer.

alex_cs: cedar asked for an ETA for disabling prefetch on their pool — can ops do that now?

sam_support: ops can toggle per-pool, will do a brief change window (1 min) and let you know when complete.

sam_support: toggled prefetch=false on cedar-dedicated-pool-07 at 2026-03-05T02:14:30Z — monitoring for regression. customer confirmed latency normalized in their tests. :thumbsup:

alex_cs: customer confirmed, thanks team. keeping ticket open for eng action items.

kai_eng: noted. I'll post findings and link PR in the Jira.

maria_pm: adding acceptance criteria to the ticket: (1) root cause analysis, (2) test case that reproduces cache thrash, (3) regression tests, (4) config guard for prefetch, (5) rollout plan.

alex_cs: closing loop with customer tonight, will keep them updated on Jira milestones.

jules_sre: leaving pointer for eng: check for race in `prefetch_worker` around `kv_load()` and `evict_threshold` logic — logs point to concurrent repopulation.

kai_eng: good call, thanks.
